newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Chubb posts H1 at low end of forecasts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Chubb posts H1 at low end of forecasts.

text.p: Britain's Chubb Security Plc on Tuesday posted first-half results at the low end of market expectations and predicted that two recent acquisitions would dilute full-year earnings by about 3.0 million pounds ($4.9 million).
The security services provider's pretax profits rose nearly four percent to 46.1 million pounds but came in at the bottom of analysts' forecasts, which ranged from 46.5 to 48.0 million.
Chief executive David Peacock said market weakness in South Africa and continental Europe hurt Chubb's first-half results.
"We had some disappointment in South Africa and Europe," he told Reuters in an interview.
"We got our callibration wrong in South Africa. We expanded, but the market was slightly out of phase with that. The situation will improve in the second half there," he added.
In continental Europe, Chubb's operating profits fell to about 0.7 million pounds from 2.2 million pounds.
"That's a continuing difficulty. The markets are projecting improvement in Germany and France, but we've got more of a wait-and-see view on that," Peacock said.
He added that analysts' forecasts for Chubb's pretax profits for the year ended March 31 averaged about 103 to 104 million pounds, excluding the dilutive effect of recent acquisitions.
Peacock declined to comment on the forecasts.

"We're confident of our position. And the continued growth of the electronic security and fire protection businesses will benefit operating profit in the second half," he said, adding that Chubb's expansion in Asia would also boost results.
Chubb shares pared their losses in morning trade as stocks in London continued to recover from the "Grey Friday" shakeout.
The company's stock was off three pence at 327.5 per share by 0950 GMT after scraping 320 earlier.

Peacock said Chubb's acquisition of James Hardie Building Services would dilute the company's earnings by about 2.0 million pounds in 1996/97, and its purchase of MSS Security would result in dilution of some 1.0 million pounds.
Chubb bought the building services firm from Australia's James Hardie Industries Ltd for about A$220 million and acquired MSS from Mayne Nickless Ltd for some A$41 million earlier this year.
Peacock said MSS would make "an important contribution" to profits in 1997/98, while James Hardie would be earnings enhancing after financing costs and before restructuring expenses for that year.
He added that the James Hardie unit would be fully earnings enhancing in 1998/99.
Peacock said Chubb was in talks for further acquisitions, but he declined to give details.

"With our good operating cash flow and our gearing, we're looking at further opportunities to deliver good value," he said, noting that the company would be very selective about any future acquisitions.
He added that Chubb expected its gearing to reach about 20 percent by the end of its financial year, including the effect of acquisitions.
The company, demerged from Racal Electronics in 1992, had net cash of some 51 million pounds at the end of the first half. ($1=.6087 Pound)
